16.22.8.en: Who will be justified against the Antichrist, who will appear more criminal than all...?!

16.22.9.en: No one is justified before (God). Abraham was righteous, and Moses and others of the famous, but if they are compared with Christ they are not counted righteous. When they come near His light their light is counted darkness, as the lamp grows dark in the rays of the sun. Thus the light of the righteous shines before man, but it does not shine before Christ. For it was not said only "Let your light shine," but "Let your light so shine before men," because the light of the righteous cannot shine before Christ].

16.23.s.en: 6. The promise to receive her anew:

16.23.0.en: 59 "For thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even deal with thee as thou hast done, which hast despised the oath in breaking the covenant. 60 Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant. 61 Then thou shalt remember thy ways, and be ashamed, when thou shalt receive thy sisters, thine elder and thy younger: and I will give them unto thee for daughters, but not by thy covenant. 62 And I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: 63 That thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame, when I pardon thee for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord GOD."

16.24.0.en: After declaring this hideous picture to Judah in her open, shameless adultery, which surpassed the evil of the Gentiles, and after offering her chastening, He turned again to open to her the door of hope in her return to Him through the New Covenant into which she enters in Christ Jesus our Lord: "I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant... And I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: that thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame, when I pardon thee for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord GOD" [60-63]. This is the everlasting covenant, in which we no longer remember our sins but find in it forgiveness for all that we have done, so that our heart rests in it forever.

16.24.1.en: I am not one among billions!

16.24.2.en: * Now I know that I am not one among the billions!

16.24.3.en: I am the object of Your love and Your personal care!

16.24.4.en: * My sin cast me on the road, and I became like a discarded thing!

16.24.5.en: There is none who looks at me, nor any who asks about me!

16.24.6.en: There is none who lifts me out of the dust of the road and its dangers!

16.24.7.en: * You passed by me, and looked upon me with Your divine gaze!

16.24.8.en: I felt the warmth of love.

16.24.9.en: I heard You whisper in my ears:

16.24.10.en: Your time is the time of love!

16.24.11.en: * You carried me on Your everlasting arms, You washed me in the waters of Baptism, You anointed me with the oil of the Myron, You have become my garment, I hide in You!

16.24.12.en: You have become my food and my drink! My wealth and my riches!

16.24.13.en: My joy and the gladness of my heart!

16.24.14.en: You shone upon me with Your splendor, so my depths became exceeding beautiful and glorious!

16.24.15.en: * You counted me a son to You, a holy bride to You, O King of kings!

16.24.16.en: You made me a queen, sitting in the heavenly places!

16.24.17.en: You made me a member of Your holy Body!

16.24.18.en: And You prepared me as a second heaven for Your joyful Kingdom!

16.24.19.en: * Who, then, cares for me as You do?!

16.24.20.en: Whom have I on earth and in heaven but You?!

16.24.21.en: I long for You, O Bridegroom of my soul!

17.0.s.en: 1. The riddle of the vine and the two eagles:

17.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, put forth a riddle, and speak a parable unto the house of Israel; 3 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; A great eagle with great wings, longwinged, broad of shoulder, full of terrors, came unto Lebanon, and took the highest branch of the cedar: 4 He cropped off the top of his young twigs, and carried it into a land of traffick; he set it in a city of merchants. 5 He took also of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful field; he placed it by great waters, and set it as a willow tree. 6 And it grew, and became a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward him, and the roots thereof were under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs. 7 There was also another great eagle with great wings and broad of shoulder: and, behold, this vine did bend her roots toward him, and shot forth her branches toward him, that he might water it by the furrows of her plantation. 8 It was planted in a good soil by great waters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine. 9 Say thou, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Shall it prosper? shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it wither? it shall wither in all the leaves of her spring, even without great power or many people to pluck it up by the roots thereof. 10 Yea, behold, being planted, shall it prosper? shall it not utterly wither, when the east wind toucheth it? it shall wither in the furrows where it grew."

17.0.1.en: The Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to put forth a riddle to the house of Israel, which bore a living and precise picture of what happened in the first captivity of Judah and the events and situations that followed it.

17.0.2.en: He said that a great eagle with great wings, thick of feathers and of divers colours, with many talons, had planned to enter Lebanon. As Origen says: [The description of the eagle here differs from that of the rest of the eagles in its huge size, its enormous wings and its strong talons, and it is planning to enter Lebanon, pluck off choice cedar branches, uproot them and take them to the land of Canaan, the city of merchants, surrounded by walls... It carries the plants out, to plant them in a field near flowing water.

17.1.0.en: The Lord made clear that this eagle is the king of Babylon [11]; his great wings and many talons are a symbol of the strength of his weapons and the vastness of his army. The thickness of his feathers and the variety of his colors point to the many kingdoms that were under his dominion. This king set it in his heart to seize Lebanon, which points to the kingdom of Judah.

17.1.1.en: Origen says of Nebuchadnezzar: [He was the great eagle, great-winged, broad of shoulder (Ezek 17:3), for he dared to say: "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the kings like a valiant man: And my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people: and as one gathereth eggs that are left, have I gathered all the earth" (Isa 10:13-14)...

17.1.2.en: This great eagle had no authority to enter Lebanon... but since they sinned before the Lord, this great eagle plucked them away, he plucked off the branches of the whole tree and carried them to Canaan, where it is said of the land of the Babylonians (the accursed, like Canaan), for Noah says: "Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren" (Gen 9:25)].

17.1.3.en: About 597 B.C. Nebuchadnezzar entered the holy city, the capital of Judah (symbolically Lebanon), after besieging it for eighteen months. What did the king do?

17.1.4.en: a. He took the highest branch of the cedar [3], or, according to the Septuagint, the choice branches of the cedar. If the cedar tree here points to the royal house of David, then its choice or lofty branch is King Jehoiachin with his family, whom he carried off to Babylon.

17.1.5.en: b. He cropped off the top of his young twigs [4], or the tops of the new branches, and entered with it into the city of merchants, pointing to his harvesting the best of the youth, those of high skills and the sons of the priests and the aristocrats, and gathering them in his net to Babylon, and he left them complete freedom to work there, so they carried on large commercial enterprises during their captivity.

17.1.6.en: c. He took of the seed of the land and planted it in a fruitful field and watered it with many waters, so it became like a willow tree [5], under whose shade many take shelter. The seed sprouted and became a spreading vine, but of low stature. Its branches turned toward the eagle to embrace him, but its roots were under him [6].

17.1.7.en: This seed is none other than King Zedekiah, the uncle of Jehoiachin, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king over Judah in place of his nephew Jehoiachin; for Nebuchadnezzar did not destroy the city nor demolish the temple, but was content with taking some of the youth with the vessels of the house of the Lord. He left Zedekiah to tend the field fruitful with many waters and to gather his people, after a treaty was made and the king swore not to betray. And indeed the seed began to grow to become a spreading vine, but of low stature because it was under the dominion of the king of Babylon. It turned its branches to embrace the eagle, that is, it entered with the king into a treaty, but its roots were under him, a sign of his authority over it.

17.1.8.en: It is of low stature, and as Origen says: [It could not be but of low stature, that which sprouted in Babylon. How could it keep its former strength, that which began to become a Babylonian vine?! The great eagle transplanted it because it had not produced fruit in the holy city. See, it settles in Canaan, so it became low in stature, feeble. When it was in the holy land it was a great vine, but when it was transplanted to the land of sinners it became weak and feeble. And you, O vine that hearest me, if you wish to be great do not go beyond the borders of the Church. Settle in the holy land, in Jerusalem, or else because of your sins you will come into a bad state and be transplanted to another land. You will become a feeble and withered vine, your fruit will fall, and your roots will dry up, and you will long for rest near the other eagle].

17.1.9.en: [Some were taken and carried off to Babylon, those who were princes in the Church; because of their sin they were removed from the top of Lebanon... Let us pray that no one may be moved from Jerusalem to Canaan, and that we may not turn away from His will, lest the branch be corrupted, and the fruit dry up together with the roots. For the planting of Jerusalem cannot bear fruit in another land, nor yield a crop in a strange land, but dries up and withers with its fruit unless it remains in the will of the Lord and in His Church, that is, in the works and commandments and the understanding of the truth of Jesus Christ].

17.1.10.en: As for the other great eagle, he is Pharaoh of Egypt; he is great-winged, a symbol of the strength of his army, and he has thick feathers, a symbol of the large number of his soldiers, but he is not of divers colors, because he does not rule over many nations as Babylon does; it is toward him that the vine bent her roots and turned her branches that he might water it as its plants grew. This vine points to King Zedekiah, who inclined, with the majority of the people, to take refuge in Pharaoh of Egypt against Nebuchadnezzar, so the king betrayed the covenant and broke the oath when he thought of revolting against the king of Babylon. Here Ezekiel warned the king of two errors: first, the breaking of the oath even if it was with a pagan king, and second, leaning on the arm of man (Pharaoh of Egypt) instead of repenting and returning to God with all the heart. He declared that Zedekiah's fate would be like that of his predecessors, Jehoahaz, who was taken captive to Egypt in 607 B.C. (Ezek 19:4), and Jehoiachin, who was taken captive to Babylon (Ezek 19:9).

17.2.0.en: When King Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar by sending his messengers to Egypt that they might give him horses and much people [15], God asks him: "Shall he prosper?" [9] and the answer came at once: "Shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it wither? it shall wither in all the leaves of her spring, even without great power or many people to pluck it up by the roots thereof. Yea, behold, being planted, shall it prosper? shall it not utterly wither, when the east wind toucheth it? it shall wither in the furrows where it grew" [9-10]. Thus He affirms more than once that the vine will wither in its roots and its fruit, in its leaves as in the furrows where it grew, that is, it will dry up completely on every level!

17.3.0.en: Origen asks why both Nebuchadnezzar and Pharaoh are called "an eagle," which is among the abominable birds (Lev 11:13), while at the same time the righteous and the good are likened to eagles. In Proverbs it is said: "Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom. Shall thine eyes fly toward it, and it is not? for it maketh itself wings; as an eagle it flieth toward heaven" (Prov 23:4-5); (the righteous man cares not for his own wisdom but makes for himself the two wings of an eagle, which are faith and works, or the love of God and the love of men, with which he flies to heaven to rest by the grace of God in the divine bosom); as it is also said: "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint" (Isa 40:31).

17.3.1.en: Origen says: [If the eagle is abominable and accursed, it is not fitting for us to take wings like the wings of an eagle when we are good, and if the riches of the rich increase, they ought not to make for themselves wings like eagles] Why, then, was the eagle used as a likeness for the good?

17.3.3.en: [There are in the Holy Bible names of some animals that can be considered good and evil at the same time...

17.3.4.en: For example, the lion has two sides: a good side: "Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up... he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him up?" (Gen 49:9). And an evil side: "Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: whom resist stedfast in the faith" (1 Pet 5:8-9). In addition to this, the crafty deceiver, wishing to make us stand and fall: "He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor" (Ps 10:9).

17.3.5.en: Thus, as we have seen, the lion can be considered from two sides, one good and the other evil, and so also the eagle...

17.3.6.en: The good man is not an eagle, but is like the eagle, because he rivals the eagle.

17.3.7.en: Likewise the bronze serpent (Num 21:8) was a type of the Savior, because it was not a real serpent but like one. It points to the Savior: "And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up" (Jn 3:14)... And in another place the good man is commanded to be wise as serpents (Mt 10:16), not that he himself should become a serpent, and that, of course, in order to avoid acquiring the deceit of the real serpent...

17.3.8.en: The eagle and the lion are among the pure creatures, for we find for the cherubim "the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle" (Ezek 1:10)... They are pure, for there is nothing unclean in the presence of God.

17.3.9.en: And you, O believer, have become pure, and what God has made pure you must not make unclean. Thus it was said to the Apostle Peter concerning everything: "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common" (Ar 10:15).

17.3.10.en: Thus the purity of the lion and the eagle that appeared with the cherubim was also declared. In addition to this, the prophecy of the coming of Christ is fulfilled by recognizing the pure lion and the pure eagle... "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox" (Isa 11:6), and that is when this is realized by faith in Christ, where the different natures are united among themselves, so the lion is not abominable but forgets its ferocity. And all the animals that are said to be abominable in the law of God receive again the nature of their former state at the beginning of creation. This transformation has already begun and will be accomplished at the Second Coming...

17.3.11.en: Do not be very astonished, then, if both Pharaoh and Nebuchadnezzar were likened to the eagle...].

17.4.0.en: 11 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 12 "Say now to the rebellious house, Know ye not what these things mean? tell them, Behold, the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the king thereof, and the princes thereof, and led them with him to Babylon; 13 And hath taken of the king's seed, and made a covenant with him, and hath taken an oath of him: he hath also taken the mighty of the land: 14 That the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping of his covenant it might stand. 15 But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people. Shall he prosper? shall he escape that doeth such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered? 16 As I live, saith the Lord GOD, surely in the place where the king dwelleth that made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant he brake, even with him in the midst of Babylon he shall die. 17 Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war, by casting up mounts, and building forts, to cut off many persons: 18 Seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand, and hath done all these things, he shall not escape. 19 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; As I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken, even it will I recompense upon his own head. 20 And I will spread my net upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon, and will plead with him there for his trespass that he hath trespassed against me. 21 And all his fugitives with all his bands shall fall by the sword, and they that remain shall be scattered toward all winds: and ye shall know that I the LORD have spoken it."

17.5.0.en: The Lord did not leave the riddles obscure but gave to the rebellious house [12] their interpretation, so that they might have no excuse in their rush to rely on Pharaoh of Egypt and his armies, and He focused in the interpretation on the gravity of breaking and violating the covenant and swearing falsely, even if it was with a pagan king, which compelled the Lord Himself to intervene to chasten them with defeat. He affirmed that the ruin does not come about by human power, but God Himself rose up against them to chasten them. He affirms:

17.5.2.en: shall he escape that doeth such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered?!

17.5.3.en: As I live, saith the Lord GOD, surely in the place where the king dwelleth that made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant he brake, even with him in the midst of Babylon he shall die.

17.5.4.en: Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war, by casting up mounts, and building forts, to cut off many persons.

17.5.5.en: Seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand, and hath done all these things, he shall not escape.

17.6.0.en: Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; As I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken, even it will I recompense upon his own head. And I will spread my net upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon, and will plead with him there for his trespass that he hath trespassed against me. And all his fugitives with all his bands shall fall by the sword, and they that remain shall be scattered toward all winds: and ye shall know that I the LORD have spoken it" [15-21].

17.6.1.en: Thus God considered the oath to be His own oath, and the breaking of it a personal insult to Him, so Pharaoh with all his armies cannot rescue him from the hand of the Lord nor from the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, and the One who catches him in His net is the Lord, who carries him to Babylon to die there for his betrayal of the covenant. He will fall, he and his counselors and his army, by the sword, and the rest of the people will be taken captive and scattered toward every wind!

17.6.2.en: Therefore the Lord Christ warned us against swearing entirely, saying: "Ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil" (Mt 5:33-37).

17.6.3.en: St. John Chrysostom warned much against the use of oaths; among his words:

17.6.4.en: [Today I am ready to show not the ruin of one house or two or three because of an oath, but the ruin of an entire city and a people beloved of God, who always enjoyed much divine care, and a race that escaped many dangers, Jerusalem itself, the city of God, which had the holy temple and all the divine service, in which were found the prophets and the grace of the Spirit and the ark and the two tablets of the covenant and the golden vessel, and which the angels often visited... it perished only because of an oath].

17.6.5.en: [It is not the oath that makes a man trustworthy, but the testimony of his life, the uprightness of his words and his good repute. Many open their throats with oaths and yet cannot persuade anyone to trust them, and others merely express their acceptance of a thing and are more worthy of belief than those who swear much].

17.6.6.en: [Truly the troubles of swearing are exceedingly great...

17.6.7.en: Since we know this, let us avoid swearing, and let our mouth practice at all times saying "believe me," and this will become a source of every godly conduct. For when the tongue is trained to use this expression alone, it becomes modest and ashamed to utter evil and wicked words].

17.6.8.en: [When we refrain from swearing entirely, we close the entrance completely before (Satan), but if we utter one oath we give him an opportunity to cause us endless harm].

17.6.9.en: St. John Chrysostom demands of us not only not to swear but also not to require others to swear, for he says:

17.6.10.en: [I ask you, are you in doubt concerning financial matters, so that you kill the soul of (your brother by asking him to swear)...?!

17.6.11.en: If you believe that he is truthful, do not oblige him to swear, and if you know that he is lying, do not force him to commit perjury].

17.7.s.en: 3. The promise of a new kingdom:

17.7.0.en: 22 "Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a branch, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent: 23 In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell. 24 And all the trees of the field shall know that I the LORD have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish: I the LORD have spoken and have done it."

17.7.1.en: If entering into a treaty with the king of Babylon helped Judah for a time, so that she became like a willow tree and like a spreading vine of low stature [5-6], and if taking refuge in Pharaoh of Egypt destroyed her completely, then there is no salvation for man by a human arm. God Himself must intervene and plant His vine with His own hands, planting it in Himself, the lofty, towering mountain, so that the enemy cannot approach it. "Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a branch, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent" [22]. He takes from the branch of the house of David (the cedar), where the Lord Christ, the Son of David, becomes incarnate, and plants the Church in Him! He is the head of the new branches, He is the branch planted not by a human arm nor from a human seed, but He is the Word of God, born before all ages, who became incarnate in the high mountain of Israel, and appears as a fruitful branch, and becomes a great cedar under which dwell the believers of every color and every tribe and tongue and nation. They fly to Him by the Holy Spirit and settle in the shadow of His branches [23]!

17.7.2.en: Thus in the midst of the dark prophecies and the severe chastenings the Lord dawns upon them with the hope of salvation by a divine arm through the Messiah, the true King, of the seed of David, who gathers into His Body members from all peoples!

17.7.3.en: God, who permitted them the two eagles, the king of Babylon and Pharaoh of Egypt, to chasten them, carries them as on the wings of an eagle, not to bring them into the Promised Land, but to carry humanity from all nations to the Father's bosom, in the heavenly Jerusalem, where eagles cannot snatch away!

17.7.4.en: Carry me as on eagles' wings!

17.7.5.en: * Of old You carried Your people from the bondage of Pharaoh as on eagles' wings, and brought them to Yourself, and led them into the Promised Land!

17.7.6.en: But when they forsook You they became prey to the eagles!

17.7.7.en: Nebuchadnezzar carried them off like an eagle devouring them, they took refuge in Pharaoh of Egypt, and behold, he was like an eagle snatching them away!

17.7.8.en: Now You have come to our world, to humanity that believes in You, carrying them as on eagles' wings to the bosom of Your Father!

17.7.9.en: * My God... how much I need You!

17.7.10.en: Behold, my sins have stirred up the eagles against me!

17.7.11.en: I fled from Your hands and became cheap prey!

17.7.12.en: Come, O wonderful in Your love, carry me in Yourself, and hide me, and cover me!

17.7.13.en: Give me the wings of a dove that I may fly to heaven!

17.7.14.en: Grant me Your Holy Spirit working in her!

17.7.15.en: May You carry me to the bosom of Your Father, O Holy One!

17.7.16.en: How I long for You, O Rock of my soul!
